question: Should current OpenClaw treat the exact disallowed-local-media-path and `Bad Request: message is too long` delivery failures as terminal queue errors after rebasing this PR?
rationale: The change intentionally stops retries for matching outbound failures; current main has a more conservative recovery model and the broader report also proposes prevention earlier in the send path.

options.title: Rebase and retain narrow terminal classification
options.body: Port the two exact patterns and regression coverage to current main as a recovery safety net, while leaving enqueue validation and splitting to separate work.

options.title: Handle only at earlier boundaries
options.body: Decline the classifier change and instead require validation or channel-side message handling before queue admission.

options.title: Broaden the error taxonomy first
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers define a provider-aware permanent-delivery-error contract beyond these two strings.

recommendation.title: Rebase and retain narrow terminal classification
recommendation.body: Port the two exact patterns and regression coverage to current main as a recovery safety net, while leaving enqueue validation and splitting to separate work.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently maintained the live PR head and recorded the focused outbound validation context.
